mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate applied to future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns through continuous monetary tightening effects.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.0), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) and declining industrial production (INDPRO < 108.0) indicates an economic downturn, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors flee risk.

failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 4.5), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
